collection_summary: Exhaustive table of the 20 standard proteinogenic amino acids encoded by the standard genetic code. The row universe is a closed, authoritative scientific set (not a curator-selected 'major/notable' list), so claim_type is exhaustive at the level of the standard genetic code. Each row carries the IUPAC three-letter and one-letter codes, a side-chain class from the standard five-category biochemical grouping, and the amino acid's essentiality status in humans (essential / conditionally essential / nonessential). Selenocysteine and pyrrolysine are deliberately out of scope because they are not encoded by the standard codon table.
source_coverage_notes:
Roles:
- source_urls[0] (Proteinogenic_amino_acid): universe (defines the closed 20-member set encoded by the standard genetic code and distinguishes them from selenocysteine/pyrrolysine) + value (IUPAC three-letter and one-letter codes). Its side-chain table also supplies per-row chemical-property evidence used as a cross-check (e.g., Tyr listed as aromatic and weakly acidic at line 322; Cys listed as polar with an acidic side-chain pKa at line 302; His listed as weak basic and aromatic at line 307). NOTE: this article also carries its own 'Essential in humans' column (gene-expression table, lines 328-355) that conflicts with source_urls[2] on three cells; that column was NOT used (see the essentiality precedence note below).
- source_urls[1] (Amino_acid): value/validation for Side-Chain Class. The article's abbreviation/property table tags each amino acid with class/polarity/charge attributes -- e.g., Tyr = Aromatic / Bronsted acid / Neutral (lines 383-408); Gly = Aliphatic / Nonpolar / Neutral (line 396); Cys = Thiol / Bronsted acid / Neutral (line 393); the charged set acidic = Asp/Glu and basic = Arg/Lys/His; His listed cationic/positive (lines 397-398). These are the source-observed properties; the single five-class label per row in the CSV (nonpolar aliphatic / aromatic / polar uncharged / positively charged (basic) / negatively charged (acidic)) is a curator normalization built on top of this evidence -- see normalization_decisions for the mapping and the scheme-dependent cases.
- source_urls[2] (Essential_amino_acid): value + PRECEDENCE source for Essential in Humans. Its human three-way classification is authoritative for this column: 'the nine amino acids humans cannot synthesize are valine, isoleucine, leucine, methionine, phenylalanine, tryptophan, threonine, histidine, and lysine' (lines 156, 163-173); conditionally essential = arginine, cysteine, glycine, glutamine, proline, tyrosine; nonessential among the standard 20 = alanine, aspartic acid, asparagine, glutamic acid, serine.
Essentiality source precedence: where source_urls[0]'s gene-expression 'Essential in humans' column conflicts with source_urls[2] (source_urls[0] marks Glutamic acid 'Conditionally' and Proline and Glutamine 'No'), source_urls[2] takes precedence. The CSV follows source_urls[2] for all three cells (Glu = Nonessential; Gln, Pro = Conditionally essential). This is intentional and not an accidental mismatch.
No non-Wiki sources were needed; the universe and every cell are grounded in the three cited Wikipedia articles. A Wiki-family discovery pass (DNA and RNA codon tables; Wikidata Q3241589) confirmed the 20-row standard-code universe but supplied no competing row table. No supplementation from individual entity pages was required (no proposed_supplements).
decision_log:
Candidate card (fast viability gate):
- Pre-gate verdict: Pass. Closed deterministic universe (20 standard amino acids), 20 rows (>= 10), one key + four non-key attributes, and a genuine confidence gradient (codes are broadly memorized; essentiality is moderately known; side-chain class is the hardest cell).
- Seed/provenance: Original. The example_questions.txt seed pool is effectively exhausted for viable picks (only #16 remains, which would over-saturate multi_attribute_projection while reusing the saturated `countries` bucket). No seed covers a biochemistry closed-set table.
- Category: multi_attribute_projection (primary). DB analog is a multi-column projection over a single closed source set with per-cell confidence varying by attribute, which matches the category definition. operation_type=projection. secondary_category=factual_lookup (each row is a per-entity attribute lookup). Category is over target (8/8 -> 9/8); accepted deliberately because all 15 categories are at/over target and entity-class novelty is the only live diversification axis per instance_selection_priorities.md.
- Source plan: Wikipedia 'Proteinogenic amino acid' (universe + codes), 'Amino acid' (side-chain groupings), 'Essential amino acid' (essentiality). Tier B manual_wikipedia.
- Expected shape: 20 rows x 5 cols, PK = Amino Acid.
- Domain: Science/Biochemistry (NEW subdomain within the already-large Science family). Entity class taxonomic-entities/amino-acids (NEW fine-class; consistent with the existing taxonomic-entities/nutrients precedent for vitamins_top5_food_sources). Entity-class novelty scores Good (NEW fine-class within an existing bucket); taxonomic-entities is mid-light (watch) but not saturated.
- Risks/adaptation: (1) Side-Chain Class is scheme-dependent across textbooks/sources -- mitigated by committing to the standard five-class grouping and documenting the scheme-dependent cases in normalization_decisions. (2) Science is the heaviest domain family -- accepted because family-level diversity is declared met and the rubric now prioritizes entity-class novelty. (3) Category over-target -- accepted as above.
- Decision: Stage.

Scope decisions: universe fixed to the standard genetic code's 20 amino acids; selenocysteine/pyrrolysine excluded (not standard-codon-encoded). Rows sorted alphabetically by amino acid name. claim_type=exhaustive is honest because the standard genetic code defines exactly these 20 -- this is not a 'major/notable' curator-bound list.
normalization_decisions: Names: full amino acid names follow Wikipedia article titles ('Aspartic acid', 'Glutamic acid' rather than the conjugate-base forms aspartate/glutamate). Codes: IUPAC standard three-letter and one-letter codes, verbatim from the Proteinogenic amino acid article. Side-Chain Class: committed to the standard five-category biochemical grouping (nonpolar aliphatic / aromatic / polar uncharged / positively charged (basic) / negatively charged (acidic)) so every cell takes exactly one categorical value on top of the per-row class/polarity/charge property tags the cited articles supply. Mapping of the scheme-dependent cases to the cited evidence: Tyrosine -> 'Aromatic', directly supported by the 'Amino acid' table tag Aromatic/Bronsted acid/Neutral (lines 383-408) and the 'Proteinogenic amino acid' listing of Tyr as aromatic and weakly acidic (line 322); the aromatic phenol side chain is grouped with the other aromatics rather than with the polar-uncharged residues. Glycine -> 'Nonpolar aliphatic', supported by the 'Amino acid' tag Aliphatic/Nonpolar/Neutral (line 396). Cysteine -> 'Polar uncharged', a normalization of the 'Amino acid' tag Thiol/Bronsted acid/Neutral (line 393) and 'Proteinogenic amino acid' evidence that the thiol side chain is polar with an acidic pKa (line 302); it is grouped with the neutral polar residues rather than the charged set. Methionine and Proline -> 'Nonpolar aliphatic'. Histidine -> 'Positively charged (basic)', per its imidazole side chain, consistent with the 'Amino acid' table listing His as cationic/positive (lines 397-398) and 'Proteinogenic amino acid' listing it as weak basic and aromatic (line 307), even though it is only partially protonated at physiological pH. The single five-class label is the curator's normalization; the underlying class/polarity/charge attributes are the source-observed values. Essential in Humans: three values exactly -- 'Essential', 'Conditionally essential', 'Nonessential' -- mapped from the Essential amino acid article (source_urls[2]), which is the authoritative precedence source for this column. The 'Proteinogenic amino acid' gene-expression table (source_urls[0], lines 328-355) carries its own 'Essential in humans' column that conflicts on three cells (it marks Glutamic acid 'Conditionally' and Proline and Glutamine 'No'); those conflicting cells were NOT used -- the CSV follows source_urls[2] (Glu = Nonessential; Gln, Pro = Conditionally essential). Selenocysteine, which the Essential amino acid article lists among nonessential, is out of scope here.
open_questions: 1. Side-Chain Class is the one normalization-sensitive column: an audit may prefer a different but equally standard scheme (e.g., placing Tyrosine under polar uncharged, or adding a separate 'sulfur-containing' class for Cys/Met). The chosen five-class scheme is documented above; a future version could split the column into orthogonal 'Polarity' and 'Charge' columns if a less scheme-dependent classification is wanted. 2. Histidine's classification (basic vs. aromatic) is a known borderline case; it is placed with the basic side chains per the cited grouping. 3. If a future benchmark version wants the broader 22 proteinogenic amino acids, selenocysteine and pyrrolysine would be added and the claim would shift from 'standard genetic code' to 'all genetically encoded'.

Fixed in curation.json prose only: source_coverage_notes now describes source_urls[1] as supplying per-row class/polarity/charge property tags (Tyr = Aromatic/Bronsted acid/Neutral; Gly = Aliphatic/Nonpolar/Neutral; Cys = Thiol/Bronsted acid/Neutral; acidic = Asp/Glu; basic = Arg/Lys/His) and explicitly separates these source-observed properties from the curator-normalized single five-class label. normalization_decisions now maps each scheme-dependent case (Tyr/Gly/Cys/Met/Pro/His) to the specific cited line evidence. No CSV value changes -- the auditor confirmed all side-chain cells are defensible under the declared scheme.

H2 (factual): essentiality source precedence was correct in the CSV but undocumented despite a visible conflict inside source_urls[0]. Fixed in curation.json prose only: added an explicit precedence note in source_coverage_notes and normalization_decisions naming source_urls[2] (Essential_amino_acid) as authoritative for the Essential in Humans column, and recording that source_urls[0]'s gene-expression 'Essential in humans' column conflicts on Glutamic acid (Conditionally), Proline (No), and Glutamine (No) and was deliberately not used. CSV follows source_urls[2] (Glu = Nonessential; Gln, Pro = Conditionally essential).
